movie.title: A Man of His Time
movie.overview: September 1940. Henri Marre arrives alone in Vichy as the authoritarian regime settles in. Broke, estranged from his family, and carrying copies of his self-published manifesto Notre Salut (Our Salvation), the 49-year-old is determined to secure what he believes is his rightful place in the new administration. In his writing, Henri sets out his patriotic convictions and his engineer’s methodology: efficiency above all. Claiming he wants to help save France after defeat, he does whatever is required to remain useful, serving the machinery of the new order with increasing skill. But he may be pursuing something more urgent: escape from his own ruin

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In September 1940, a desperate and estranged engineer arrives in Vichy determined to offer his ruthless efficiency to the new authoritarian regime to secure his own salvation.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Broke and isolated, 49-year-old Henri Marre travels to Vichy in late 1940 carrying his self-published patriotic manifesto, *Notre Salut*. Desperate to re-establish his standing and escape personal ruin, he pitches his rigorous engineer's methodology to the burgeoning administrative state. As he commits to serving the authoritarian government with increasing skill, his relentless focus on efficiency masks a deeply personal struggle for survival.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In September 1940, against the backdrop of France's recent defeat, Henri Marre arrives alone in Vichy as an authoritarian government takes root. At 49, Henri is broke, estranged from his family, and facing complete personal and financial ruin. Carrying copies of his self-published manifesto, *Notre Salut*, he seeks an audience with the new administration to present his vision for national recovery. Henri believes that France can be saved through an engineer’s absolute commitment to efficiency and methodical organization. Driven by ambition and a desire to secure what he views as his rightful position, he willingly integrates himself into the state's expanding administrative machinery. As he navigates the complex bureaucracy, Henri demonstrates an uncanny ability to make himself indispensably useful to the regime. However, his relentless devotion to duty and bureaucratic skill hide a far more urgent motive: a desperate attempt to flee the wreckage of his former life. Ultimately, Henri's calculated service to the new order reflects the chilling intersection of personal desperation and systemic compliance.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set in September 1940, *A Man of His Time* follows Henri Marre, a broke, 49-year-old engineer who arrives in Vichy just as the authoritarian regime consolidates power following France's defeat. Carrying his self-published manifesto *Notre Salut* (*Our Salvation*), Henri seeks to secure a prominent position within the new government. Estranged from his family and teetering on personal ruin, he pitches his unique methodology—one centered on absolute efficiency and bureaucratic precision—as the key to restoring the nation. As he proves his usefulness to the new order, Henri plunges deeper into the regime's machinery, balancing his ostensible patriotic convictions with a desperate, personal quest for survival and self-preservation.

story_structure.climax: Henri faces a critical turning point where his ambition for self-preservation and bureaucratic utility directly collides with the reality of the regime he serves.
story_structure.conflict: Driven by patriotic convictions, engineering efficiency, and a desperate need to escape his personal ruin, Henri seeks to prove his worth to an oppressive state that demands total compliance.
story_structure.resolution: Henri confronts the ultimate consequences of his choices, revealing whether his pragmatic service yielded true salvation or permanent moral and personal compromise.
story_structure.introduction: In September 1940, 49-year-old Henri Marre arrives broke and isolated in Vichy during the emergence of the authoritarian regime, armed with his self-published manifesto 'Notre Salut' and an unshakable drive to secure a role in the new administration.
story_structure.risingAction: Henri increasingly integrates himself into the machinery of the Vichy government, adapting his skills and doing whatever is necessary to remain indispensable as the state's demands escalate.
